open.repro_summary: GET /api/search?author=a&q=test&sort=asc&limit=10 returns a raw Postgres syntax error revealing SQL injection in the sort parameter.
open.summary: The 'sort' parameter of /api/search is concatenated directly into a SQL query without sanitization, causing a database syntax error when injected with 'asc' variants.

open.repro_summary: GET /api/search?q=a&sort=asc)%3B-- returns SQLSTATE 42601 syntax error, indicating injected SQL fragment reached the database parser.
open.summary: Injecting payload 'asc);--' into the sort parameter triggers a raw SQL syntax error, confirming unsanitized use of user input in a query and potential for stacked/comment-based injection.

open.repro_summary: GET /api/search?sort=id)--%20 returns a Postgres syntax error for unexpected ')' character.
open.summary: The sort parameter accepts raw SQL syntax including closing parentheses and comment sequences, causing a database-level syntax error and confirming injectable query construction.

open.repro_summary: Any malformed 'sort' value returns verbose Postgres error text in the JSON response body.
open.summary: Raw database error messages (including SQLSTATE codes and query syntax details) are returned directly to the client, leaking backend implementation details.

open.repro_summary: GET /api/search?author=cmp-rehearsal&q=&sort=id--&limit=5 returns results in reversed order compared to the same query without the injected comment, proving the injected SQL comment altered query execution.
open.summary: Appending SQL comment syntax '--' after a valid sort column value ('id--') is accepted by the server and changes the ORDER BY direction/behavior, confirming the sort parameter is used unsanitized and comment-truncation injection works.
